tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Model Kits
tips.text: To remove old paint from model kits, first soften the paint using an appropriate solvent like Tamiya Acetone or Vallejo Airbrush Cleaner. Apply with a brush, let it soak for 5-10 minutes, then gently scrape off the softened paint with a plastic scalpel or toothpick. For stubborn areas, use a dental pick or needle under the paint edge to lift it off. Always work in a well-ventilated area.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To fix broken photo-etch parts, use a minimal amount of CA glue like Mr. Hobby Super Fast Clear or Revell Contacta. Apply a small drop on the inside of the joint, let it wick in, then quickly align the parts and hold them together with tweezers until set. For stronger repairs, use a tiny bit of super glue like Loctite Gel Control. Always use with proper ventilation.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To recover a clogged airbrush, first disassemble it according to the manufacturer's instructions (e.g., Iwata, Badger). Soak the nozzle, needle, and other parts in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner or Iwata Airbrush Cleaner for 10-15 minutes. Gently scrub with a soft brush, then reassemble the airbrush and test spray. If still clogged, use a needle-cleaning tool to clear the nozzle and needle.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: To avoid frost from rattle cans, spray in well-ventilated areas, preferably above 60°F (15°C). Shake the can vigorously for at least 1 minute before spraying. Hold the can upright and maintain a consistent distance (8-10 inches) from the model. For best results, use a primer specifically designed for your paint type, like Vallejo Surface Primer or Tamiya Fine Surface Primer. Always follow manufacturer guidelines for thinning and application.
